# Woo Hoo Media Labs

> Woo Hoo Media Labs is an AI-native film and content production studio based in Mumbai, India, founded by Chntan N. Shah in 2009. The studio makes brand films, ad films and TV commercials, AI-generated commercials, government communication films, product films, and viral social content. It combines 26 years of traditional cinematic craft with a proprietary generative-AI production pipeline, delivering broadcast- and advertising-grade work for clients across India and worldwide.

## About

- [About the studio](https://woohoomedialabs.com/#about): Founded 2009 in Mumbai by Chntan N. Shah. 200+ clients served. 1000+ films released. One of India's first AI-native production studios.
- [Founder Chntan N. Shah](https://www.linkedin.com/in/chntan/): 26 years in cinema. Began in corporate and government communication filmmaking, then pivoted the studio to an AI-native production model.

## Services

- Brand films and corporate anthems
- Advertising films and TV commercials (30 / 60 / 90-second spots for broadcast and digital)
- AI-native cinema and generative narrative shorts
- Government communication films (Government of Maharashtra, Government of India)
- Product launch films and demo reels
- Episodic social formats and viral content series
- Healthcare and lifestyle brand films
- Biography and milestone films

## Notable Films

- Bhai, Shirt Pehen Lo: AI Salman Khan tribute reel — 1.2M+ Instagram views.
- Virat Kohli AI Reel: AI-generated cricket fan film — 170K+ views.
- 78-Second AI Film with 11 Characters: India's longest AI narrative brand film.
- The Shrinking Bill: AI ad film for the Norwood CRIZA BLDC fan range.
- Speed 4 Defence — Built for the Battlefield: AI-native defence brand film.
- PRATIKAR I: brand film for India's autonomous drone interceptor (Aerotronics India).

## How we produce

Woo Hoo Media Labs runs a proprietary AI-native production pipeline spanning generative video, image synthesis, character-consistency systems, voice, and original score — finished with professional editing and colour grading. The tools are treated as a production language; the deliverable is directed, broadcast-grade cinema.
